chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

For the al-mudiḥah, there are five camels. For the as-simḥaq, which is below the al-mudiḥah, there are four camels. For the al-munaqqilah, there are fifteen camels. For the al-jaʾifah, there is one-third of the blood money: thirty-three camels. And for the al-maʾmumah, there is one-third of the blood money.

key_terms.السِّمْحَاقِ: a wound beneath the skin layer and below the level of al-mudiḥah
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit used here for legal compensation
key_terms.الْجَائِفَةِ: a penetrating wound reaching the inner cavity of the body
key_terms.الْمَأْمُومَةِ: a head wound reaching the membrane surrounding the brain
key_terms.الْمُنَقِّلَةِ: a wound involving displacement or breaking of bone
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.ثُلُثُ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the full blood money compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed blood money for different types of wounds in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fixed legal compensations for specific categories of wounds and head injuries in the law of blood money. It identifies the prescribed diyah amounts for al-mudiḥah, as-simḥaq, al-munaqqilah, al-jaʾifah, and al-maʾmumah, showing the structured nature of injury compensation in fiqh.
